katas.title: requireRole: switch from role lists to role ranks so new roles slot in

seededDefectKey.scenario: A warehouse_associate calls a purchasing route guarded by requireRole(['buyer', 'warehouse_manager', 'admin']).
seededDefectKey.consequence: The guard collapses the list to 'rank >= 1', and warehouse_associate shares buyer's rank, so the associate passes a gate whose role list does not name them. The 403 body still advertises requiredRoles = the list, so the rule enforced and the rule reported disagree.

seededDefectKey.scenario: A route guarded only by a misspelled role, or a user whose role string is misspelled.
seededDefectKey.consequence: Unknown required roles become rank 99 (locks out everyone, admin included) while unknown user roles silently become rank 0; typos fail in opposite directions instead of failing loudly.

seededDefectKey.scenario: The shipped guard is exactly this rank form.
seededDefectKey.consequence: Feature doc finding 2: 'If the intent is ranking, accept one minimum role; if the intent is a list, check membership (allowedRoles.includes(role))'. No test exercises requireRole, so nothing catches it.

tests.name: a warehouse_associate cannot pass a buyer/manager/admin gate
tests.code: const g = mod.requireRole(['buyer', 'warehouse_manager', 'admin']); const r = mod.runGuard(g, 'warehouse_associate'); assert.equal(r.status, 403); assert.equal(r.nextCalled, false);

tests.name: listed roles pass and an anonymous actor is a viewer
tests.code: const g = mod.requireRole(['buyer', 'warehouse_manager', 'admin']); assert.equal(mod.runGuard(g, 'buyer').nextCalled, true); assert.equal(mod.runGuard(g, 'admin').nextCalled, true); assert.equal(mod.runGuard(g, null).status, 403);
